paper.title: ARG: Testing Query Rewriters via Abstract Rule Guided Fuzzing
paper.venue: International Conference on Automated Software Engineering

summary.text: ARG fuzzes query rewriters, the components that transform a query into a faster but semantically equivalent form. The authors argue that general DBMS testing approaches cover only a limited subset of rewrite scenarios given the diversity of rewrite rules. ARG uses abstract rules — a unified representation of the AST patterns and constraints that trigger a rewrite, plus the resulting transformation — as coverage feedback, steering generation toward patterns not yet exercised. Testing Apache Calcite, WeTune, SQLSolver and LearnedRewrite it found 38 previously unknown bugs.
summary.relationship_to_sqlancer: Measures itself directly against SQLancer, reporting more triggered rewrite rules and 15 more bugs than SQLancer in 24 hours.
supporting_excerpts: However, due to the diversity of rewrite rules, they cover only a limited subset of rewrite scenarios, potentially overlooking critical bugs.In this paper, we propose Abstract Rule Guided (ARG) fuzzing to detect bugs in query rewrites.
The key idea is to use feedback from abstract rules to guide query generation, thereby activating more rewriting logic and enhancing bug detection.
In 24 hours, ARG triggered 76% and 1017% more written rules, triggered 13 and 15 more bugs than SQLsmith and SQLancer, respectively.

sources.excerpt: Recent works have also adopted metamorphic testing to construct semantically equivalent queries to test DBMSs. NoREC [18] converts an optimizable query into a non-optimizable form of the query, then identifies logic bugs by comparing their execution results.

sources.excerpt: Similarly, TLP [19] employs ternary logic to generate three equivalent queries combined via UNION operations.
